question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

I think I might take (French leave) this afternoon and go to the cinema.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The bracketed idiom **"French leave**" refers to the act of leaving a gathering without notifying the host or obtaining permission. (बिना बताए चले जाना).
 
• The correct meaning is** "Absence without permission.**"(बिना अनुमति की अनुपस्थिति).

Therefore, the** correct ****answer** is- *'Absence without permission'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: **"To try hard"** means to put in a significant effort or struggle towards achieving something.(मेहनत करना, प्रयास करना).
 
• Option 3: **"To be inconsistent"** refers to not staying the same throughout.(अस्थिर होना).
 
• Option 4: **"To have a slight encounter"** refers to having a brief or casual meeting with someone.(संक्षिप्त मुलाकात).

1cf:T86a,
The correct answer is **'Option 1'**
